score.note: First structural draft, not a permutation search. Read games/gs1/asm/080dc6bc.s and out/family-transplants/main-080dc6bc/m2c/target.canonical.s in full and hand-derived the whole control-flow/field shape from the retained assembly (the transplant workspace's top-level 080dc6bc.c was only the member_orbit template with the symbol renamed and was not used as source). The shared-family prologue/epilogue and the two Func_080ed408(kind,7,7,c,d)/heap_cache[7]/heap_cache[8] rectangle-callback reads match the assigned template (main:080ce85c, score 8895/10000) exactly, but the body is a different effect entirely: a 64-entry, 28-byte particle table seeded at work+0x7080 (same base and record size as the already-adopted puff_arc/run.c Puff array) with a random polar offset per particle, then 96 frames that walk the member list and, for a member whose 40-frame window is open, draw its 6-particle group through one of two cached rectangle callbacks. Three real structural bugs found and fixed by reading the aligned diff, in order of value: (1) writing the particle-group pointer as ordinary `Particle *` pointer arithmetic (`base_particle_array + base_idx`) let this compiler's loop-strength-reduction turn the per-member `base_idx += 6` accumulator into a pre-multiplied `+= 168` byte-stride induction variable -- the reference instead recomputes `base_idx*28` fresh at each use via an explicit `(base_idx<<3 - base_idx)<<2` shift-sub-shift sequence with `base_idx` itself staying a plain +=6 memory scalar; spelling the multiply out in C the same way (`(base_idx << 3) - base_idx) * 4`) defeated the induction-variable rewrite and was the single largest fix: candidate_bytes 680->684 (byte-count exact), differing_halfwords 234->173. (2) Swapping the two velocity-field multiplications from `magnitude * Func_08002322(angle)` to `Func_08002322(angle) * magnitude` (and the sine equivalent) flipped which operand this compiler copies into the destination register before the `muls`, matching the reference's own `adds r3,r6,#0 / muls r3,r0` shape instead of the reverse; differing_halfwords 173->169. (3) Tried moving `member = 0` before the member-count guard to match the reference's own unconditional pre-guard `str r2,[sp,#20]` -- this is a real, observed reference scheduling choice, but on this owner's actual register/frame layout it scored slightly worse (differing_halfwords 234->237 measured against the pre-fix-(1) baseline) rather than better, so it was reverted and left as the original if-scoped declaration. All immediate operands, branch conditions, and call targets in the current aligned diff match the reference exactly; every remaining `!`/`+`/`-` line is either a register-letter swap or a stack-slot-offset shift downstream of one root cause (see family.register_finding below), or a scheduling reorder of independently-valued immediate loads (the `(clamped*9<<7)+0x1B00` source-address computation for the slot-5 draw call is emitted in a different but net-equivalent instruction order, same instruction count both sides) -- exactly the two residual classes this family's dossiers already document as not source-shape-controllable, so neither was chased further.

family.template_note: The prologue (cursor-advance work/draw_destination read, work+0x7828 state publish, Func_080cd594(0)) and epilogue (Func_08004278/Func_08002dd8 x2/Func_080cdbc0) match the template's shape exactly, and the two Func_080ed408(kind,7,7,c,d) + heap_cache[kind-39] rectangle-callback reads are the same idiom -- but the template's own body (a per-member orbiting-sprite draw driven by a 160-entry sine scanline table, two Func_080041d8 periodic-callback registrations, a member_count*16+48 frame count) does not appear here at all. This owner is 684 bytes vs the template's 724 and has a materially different, shorter body: a single Func_080041d8 registration, a fixed 96-frame loop, and a 64-entry particle table with random-polar-offset physics that the template has no equivalent of.
family.actual_sibling_evidence: The real body matches the 0x03001eec 'battle work' subsystem documented at games/gs1/recon/en/main/080e7404.c, 080d59b0.c, 080d82b0.c, 080dc1ec.c, 080e01e4.c, and especially the already-adopted games/gs1/src/battle/effects/puff_arc/run.c: same work+0x7080 28-byte-record particle table base address and record size as puff_arc's Puff array (x,y,unk08,unk0C,unk10,unk14,tick), same heap_cache[kind-39] (Data_03001e50-equivalent) rectangle-callback cache, same work+0x7780/0x7784/0x7824/0x7828 scalar fields, same *(s32*)0x03001E80 'facing' global, same Func_080049ac/Func_080051d8/Func_08004cb4 per-member portrait-setup triple already established (with an identical single-argument Func_08004cb4(record) call) in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080d59b0.c's dossier, and the same count-at-+20/id-array-at-+36 effect-state layout as puff_arc's Efx struct (cnt, actors[8]).
family.register_finding: The dominant remaining residual is this compiler choosing r9 for 'work' where the reference keeps it in sl for the whole function (visible from the very first `mov sl,r1` vs candidate's `mov r9,r1`), with 'work'-relative address adds (`add rX,sl` vs `add rX,r9`) and a knock-on loop-counter role swap (particle-init 'i' and the inner draw loop's 'slot' counter: reference reuses r9 for both non-overlapping roles, candidate uses sl) accounting for the large majority of the remaining differing_halfwords. This is the same 'register allocator keeps a loop-invariant address in a different high register' class already documented as not source-shape-controllable elsewhere in this family (member_orbit/080dc1ec/080d59b0 dossiers); declaring `work` first among the locals and scoping the early-dead `palette`/`status`/`particle`/`i` locals into narrower blocks were both tried and had zero measured effect (still 169/156), consistent with that precedent, so neither was kept as a source change.
family.call_convention_note: `bl Func_080072f0` (the WordCopyFn palette-blit) and `bl Func_080072f4` (both DrawRectangleFn draw calls) are the r3 and r4 entries of the fourteen-slot `_call_via_rN` trampoline bundle at games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s (`bx rN; mov r8,r8` at 0x080072e4+4*N, N=r0..sp), not real functions named Func_080072f0/Func_080072f4 -- confirmed the same way 080dc1ec.json/080d59b0.json already derived it (arm_function_arg in alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c never places an argument in r4; tracing the r3/r4 values back to their origin shows a WordCopyFn pool constant and the two cached heap_cache[7]/heap_cache[8] rectangle pointers respectively) and modeled the same way the already-adopted member_orbit/run.c does, as direct casts-and-calls through function-pointer values.

rejected_experiments: Ordinary `Particle *` pointer arithmetic for the group base (`(Particle*)(work+0x7080) + base_idx`): compiles correctly but this compiler's loop-strength-reduction rewrites the per-member `base_idx += 6` accumulator into a pre-scaled `+= 168` byte induction variable instead of the reference's plain `+= 6` scalar with a fresh `(x<<3-x)<<2` multiply at each use; cost 4 candidate_bytes and regressed differing_halfwords from 173 to 234 relative to the fix. Superseded by writing the `(base_idx << 3) - base_idx) * 4` byte-offset expression directly, which reproduces the reference's shift-sub-shift sequence and defeats the induction-variable rewrite.

Hoisting `member = 0` before the member-count guard (matching the reference's own unconditional `str r2,[sp,#20]` scheduling immediately after `facing`): scored differing_halfwords 237 vs 234 on the pre-fix-(1) baseline, a small regression rather than an improvement; reverted to the if-scoped declaration.

Scoping `palette`/`status` and `particle`/`i` into narrower nested blocks to shrink their live ranges ahead of the member-walk loop, hoping to relieve the register pressure behind the sl/r9 work-register swap: zero measured effect (169/156 both ways). Reverted to flat top-of-function declarations matching sibling style.

Declaring `work` as the first local instead of after `heap_cache`/`cursor`: zero measured effect on the sl/r9 assignment (169/156 both ways). Reverted to the more natural heap_cache/cursor/work/draw_destination declaration order.

Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect from the 0x03001eec work-block subsystem. Seeds a 64-entry, 28-byte particle table at work+0x7080 with a random polar offset per particle (masked 16-bit angle, masked 8-bit magnitude via Func_08004458, converted through Func_08002322/Func_0800231c; a modulo-6 'element' of 5 gets a zeroed offset instead of a computed one), loads a palette and BG2/BG3-format sprite sheet into the work block via a WordCopyFn trampoline call, opens two rectangle-blit heap kinds (46 and 47), then runs 96 frames. Each frame replays the shared facing/portrait setup for every listed party member and, for a member whose 40-frame window [member*8, member*8+40) is currently open, walks that member's six-particle sub-group (base index member*6 into the shared 64-entry table) and draws each particle through one of the two cached rectangle callbacks, selecting the callback and a growth-animation source-sprite-sheet offset (0..5, clamped) by the particle's own per-render tick counter, with the group's sixth particle (slot 5) drawn from a second sprite sheet 0x1B00 bytes further into the work block through the kind-46 callback while the other five draw from the base sheet through kind-47.

The particle table's unk0C/unk10 fields (the polar-offset x/y computed at spawn) are written once at init and never read again anywhere in this owner's own retained instructions; only the tick field (+24) is read and incremented per render. This is consistent with -- not contradicted by -- the shared Func_080041d8((void*)0x080CD261, 0x480) periodic callback already treated as an opaque, unrecovered external routine by every sibling in this family; no claim is made here about what that callback does with the table.
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
